verdict.rationale: Grok Build ships its own recurring schedule: `/loop` reruns a prompt on an interval, and background monitors can watch logs or CI runs and raise notifications. Auto mode can approve safe tools without prompting. However, this all runs inside a live conversation, not as a persistent always-on agent, and the loop example only reports failures rather than fixing them. Headless mode could be driven by an external scheduler, but that is a user-side workaround and earns no credit. Missing for 10: persistent always-on agents that run outside an interactive session, event triggers (e.g. CI or repo events) that start agent runs, documented autonomous fix workflows, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can set up always-on agents that run on schedules or triggers to maintain and fix my software autonomously

citations.quote: `/loop` runs a prompt on a recurring interval
/loop 5m Check if the test suite passes and report any failures
Grok can run commands, subagents, and monitors in the background while the conversation continues.
each line the script prints becomes a notification in the conversation. Ask for one when you want to watch a log, a CI run, or a port
